summary: 哥斯达黎加的牧场和再生林表明，有些猴类能够利用人类改变过的栖息地，尤其是取食树叶的吼猴。墨西哥可可种植园中的吼猴还能传播树种，提示保留遮阴树有助于兼顾生产和保护。
logic: 比较国家公园的猴群变化
可可种植园提供栖息地

paragraphs.brief: 牧场防风林为吼猴留出生境
sentences: Hacienda La Pacifica, a remote working cattle ranch in Guanacaste Province of northern Costa Rica, has for decades been home to a community of mantled howler monkeys.
哥斯达黎加北部瓜纳卡斯特省有一处偏远的牧牛场，名叫拉帕西菲卡，几十年来一直是一个鬃毛吼猴群的家。

Other native primates—white-faced capuchin monkeys and spider monkeys—were once common in this area too, but vanished after the Pan-American Highway was built nearby in the 1950s and most of the surrounding land was cleared for cattle-raising.
白面卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴等本地灵长类动物曾经也很常见，但20世纪50年代附近修通泛美公路、周边大部分土地被清作牧场后，它们便消失了。
At Hacienda La Pacifica, however, an enlightened ranch owner chose to leave some strips of native trees growing.
不过，拉帕西菲卡的牧场主有远见，保留了几条由本地树木组成的林带。
He used these as windbreaks to protect both cattle and their food crops from dry-season winds.
他利用这些林带挡风，让牛群和饲料作物免遭旱季强风侵袭。
In the process, the farmer unwittingly founded a unique laboratory for the study of monkeys.
在这一过程中，农民无意中建立了一个研究猴子的独特实验室。
paragraphs.gist: 哥斯达黎加牧场为牲畜和饲料作物保留防风林，附近猴群因开路清地而消失时，这些林带却给鬃毛吼猴留下了栖息地。

paragraphs.brief: 牧场边缘的再生林研究
sentences: Ken Glander, a primatologist from Duke University in the USA, is studying La Pacifica’s monkeys in an effort to understand the relationship between howlers and regenerating forests at the edges of grazing lands.
美国杜克大学灵长类动物学家肯·格兰德正在研究拉帕西菲卡的猴子，想弄清吼猴与牧地边缘再生森林的关系。
Studying such disturbed woodlands is increasingly important because throughout much of the New World Tropics, these are the only forests left.
美洲热带许多地区只剩下这类受过干扰的林地，研究它们因而愈发重要。
In the 18th century, tropical dry forests once covered most of Central America, but by the 1980s less than two percent remained undisturbed, and less than one percent was protected.
18世纪时，热带干林曾覆盖中美洲大部分地区，但到了20世纪80年代，未受干扰的已不足原有面积的2%，受保护的更不到1%。
paragraphs.gist: 格兰德研究牧场边缘再生林与吼猴的关系，因为中美洲原有热带干林到20世纪80年代已很少有未经干扰的部分。

paragraphs.brief: 食叶吼猴如何利用次生林
sentences: Howlers persist at La Pacifica, Glander explains, because they are leaf-eaters.
格兰德解释说，吼猴能在拉帕西菲卡生存下来，是因为它们以树叶为食。
They eat fruit when it is available but, unlike capuchin and spider monkeys, do not depend on large areas of fruiting trees.
有水果时它们也会吃，但不像卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴那样依赖大面积的结果树木。
Glander is particularly interested in howlers’ ability to thrive on leaves loaded with toxins—poisonous substances designed to protect the plants.
格兰德尤其感兴趣的是，吼猴如何靠富含毒素的叶子生存繁衍；这些有毒物质原本是植物的防御手段。
For leaf-eaters, long-term exposure to a specific plant toxin can increase their ability to neutralise the poisonous substances and absorb the leaf nutrients.
食叶动物长期接触某一种植物毒素，可提高中和有毒物质、吸收叶片养分的能力。

Watching generations of howlers at La Pacifica has shown Glander that the monkeys keep their systems primed by sampling a variety of plants and then focusing on a small number of the most nutritious food items.
格兰德观察了几代吼猴，发现它们先尝食多种植物，使身体保持应对毒素的能力，再集中吃少数营养最丰富的食物。
The leaves that grow in regenerating forests, like those at La Pacifica, are actually more howler-friendly than those produced by the centuries-old trees that survive farther south.
拉帕西菲卡这类再生林里的树叶，其实比更南方那些数百年树龄的老树所长的叶子更适合吼猴。
In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.
在较年轻的森林中，树木将大部分有限的能量投入到生长的木材、树叶和水果中，因此，它们产生的毒素水平远低于成熟的老树。
paragraphs.gist: 吼猴能通过尝食多种植物维持处理毒素的能力，再生林里的幼树又把更多能量用于生长，叶片毒素较少，适合它们取食。

paragraphs.brief: 森林恢复与三类猴群回归
sentences: The value of maturing forests to primates is also a subject of study at Santa Rosa National Park, about 35 miles northwest of La Pacifica.
在拉帕西菲卡西北约35英里的圣罗莎国家公园，研究者也在考察逐渐成熟的森林对灵长类动物的价值。
Large areas of Santa Rosa’s forests had at one time been burnt to make space for cattle ranching and coffee farming, thereby devastating local monkey habitat.
圣罗莎的大片森林曾一度被烧毁，为牧牛和咖啡种植创造了空间，从而摧毁了当地的猴子生境。
But in 1971 the government protected the area by designating it a national park, and species of indigenous trees which had been absent for decades began to invade the abandoned pastures.
1971年，政府将此地划为国家公园予以保护，消失数十年的本土树种开始重新长进废弃牧场。
Capuchins were the first to begin using the reborn forests, followed by howlers.
卷尾猴最先利用新生的森林，随后是吼猴。
Eventually, even spider monkeys, fruit-eaters that need large areas of continuous forest, returned.
最后，连需要大片连片森林来觅食水果的蜘蛛猴也回来了。
In the first 28 years following protection of the area, the capuchin population doubled, while the number of howlers increased seven-fold.
在当地受保护后的头28年里，卷尾猴数量增加到原来的两倍，吼猴则达到原来的七倍。
paragraphs.gist: 圣罗莎禁止砍伐放牧后，本土树木逐渐重返牧场，卷尾猴、吼猴相继回来，最后连需要大片连片森林的蜘蛛猴也回来了。

sentences: Some of the same traits that allow howlers to survive at La Pacifica also explain their population boom in Santa Rosa.
使吼猴得以在拉帕西菲卡生存的一些特征，也解释了它们在圣罗莎的数量为何激增。
Howler reproduction is faster than that of other native monkey species.
吼猴的繁殖速度快于其他本地猴种。
They give birth for the first time at about 3.5 years of age, compared with seven years for capuchins, and eight or more for spider monkeys.
吼猴约3.5岁便第一次产仔，卷尾猴约要到7岁，蜘蛛猴则要到8岁或更晚。
Also, while a female spider monkey will have a baby about once every four years, well-fed howlers can produce an infant every two years.
雌性蜘蛛猴大约每四年产一仔，而食物充足的吼猴每两年便能产一仔。
Another factor is diet.
另一个因素是饮食。
Howlers are very adaptable feeders and need only a comparatively small home range.
吼猴在取食方面适应性强，只需相对较小的活动范围。
Spider monkeys, on the other hand, need to occupy a huge home range.
蜘蛛猴则需要很大的活动范围。
Also crucial is the fact that the leaves howlers eat hold plenty of water, so the monkeys can survive away from open streams and water-holes.
还有一点很重要，吼猴吃的叶子含有充足水分，因此远离溪流和水潭也能生存。
This ability gives them a real advantage over capuchin and spider monkeys, which have suffered during the long, ongoing drought in the area.
这使吼猴比卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴更有优势，后两者已深受当地持续干旱之苦。
paragraphs.gist: 吼猴性成熟早、产仔间隔短，觅食范围小，又能从树叶中获得水分，因此在长期干旱中比其他猴类更容易繁衍。

paragraphs.brief: 可可园里的遮阴树与吼猴
sentences: Alejandro Estrada, an ecologist at Estación de Biología Los Tuxtlas in Veracruz, Mexico, has been studying the ecology of a group of howler monkeys that thrive in a habitat totally altered by humans: a cacao plantation in Tabasco State, Mexico.
墨西哥韦拉克鲁斯州洛斯图斯特拉斯生物站的生态学家亚历杭德罗·埃斯特拉达研究着一群吼猴，它们在一处完全被人类改变的环境里繁衍，即墨西哥塔巴斯科州的一座可可种植园。
Cacao plants need shade to grow, so 40 years ago the owners of Cholula Cacao Farm planted figs, monkey-pod and other tall trees to form a protective canopy over their crop.
可可树需要荫蔽，乔卢拉可可农场的主人早在40年前便种下无花果树、雨树等高大树木，让树冠为作物遮阴。
The howlers moved in about 25 years ago after nearby forests were cut.
大约25年前，周围森林被砍伐后，吼猴迁入了农场。
This strange habitat seems to support about as many monkeys as would a same-sized patch of wild forest.
这片特殊栖息地能养活的猴子数量，看来与同样面积的野生森林相当。
The howlers eat the leaves and fruit of the shade trees, leaving the valuable cacao pods alone.
吼猴以遮阴树的叶和果实为食，并不碰珍贵的可可荚。
paragraphs.gist: 墨西哥一处可可园为遮阴种下高树，吼猴迁入后以树叶和果实为食，不碰可可荚，同面积下数量与野林相当。

sentences: Estrada believes the monkeys bring under-appreciated benefits to such plantations, dispersing the seeds of fruits such as fig and other shade trees, and fertilising the soil.
埃斯特拉达认为，猴群为这类种植园带来的好处常被低估，例如传播无花果等遮阴树的种子，并使土壤更肥沃。
Spider monkeys also forage for fruit here, though they need nearby areas of forest to survive in the long term.
蜘蛛猴也来这里觅食水果，不过要长期生存，它们还需要附近有森林。
He hopes that farmers will begin to see the advantages of associating with wild monkeys, which could include potential ecotourism projects.
他希望农民渐渐认识到与野猴共存的好处，其中还可能包括开展生态旅游。
‘Conservation is usually viewed as a conflict between farming practices and the need to preserve nature,’ Estrada says.
埃斯特拉达说，过去人们谈到自然保护，通常会想到农业经营与保护环境之间的冲突。
‘We’re moving away from that vision and beginning to consider ways in which commercial activities may become a tool for the conservation of primates in human-modified landscapes.’
“我们正逐渐摆脱这种看法，开始思考商业活动如何帮助保护人类改造环境中的灵长类动物。”
paragraphs.gist: 埃斯特拉达认为，猴子能为农园传播树种、肥沃土壤，并带来生态旅游机会，使农业经营与保护灵长动物有望互相促进。

items.en: a reason why newer forests provide howlers with better feeding opportunities than older forests
items.zh: 为什么再生林比老林为吼猴提供了更有利的觅食条件。
items.why: 题干问“为何新生林比老林提供更好的取食机会*。关键点是“毒素更低 (lower levels of toxin)”,叶子对食叶的吼猴更友好。

items.en: a reference to a change in farmers’ attitudes towards wildlife
items.zh: 提到农民对野生生物态度的改变
items.why: 这里明确提到从“对立” 转向“合作"一农民/商业活动的态度正在改变 (towards wildlife conservation).

items.en: a description of the means by which howlers select the best available diet for themselves
items.zh: 说明吼猴如何从可获得的食物中挑选最适合自己的食物。
items.why: 题干要求“描述吼猴如何为自己选择最佳食物"。先“采样多种植物",再“集中于营养最好的少数种类”。

items.en: figures relating to the reduction of natural wildlife habitat over a period of time
items.zh: 一段时期内野生动物天然栖息地减少的统计数字。
items.why: 十八世纪热带干林覆盖中美洲大部分地区，到了二十世纪八十年代，未受扰动者已不到百分之二。

items.en: Howler monkeys have a more rapid rate of ________ than either capuchin or spider monkeys.
items.zh: 吼猴的________速度比卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴都快。
items.why: 回到对应内容“吼猴的繁殖速度快于其他本地猴种”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Unlike the other local monkey species, howlers can survive without eating ________ and so can live inside a relatively small habitat area.
items.zh: 与当地其他猴类不同，吼猴即使不吃________也能生存，因此可以生活在相对较小的栖息地里。
items.why: 回到对应内容“有水果时它们也会吃，但不像卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴那样依赖大面积的结果树木”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Their diet is more flexible, and they are able to tolerate leaves with high levels of ________.
items.zh: 吼猴的食谱更为灵活，即使叶子中________含量很高，它们也能耐受。
items.why: 回到对应内容“格兰德尤其感兴趣的是，吼猴如何靠富含毒素的叶子生存繁衍；这些有毒物质原本是植物的防御手段”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Howlers can also survive periods of ________ better than the other monkey species can.
items.zh: 在发生________的时期，吼猴也比其他猴类更容易存活。
items.why: 能在干旱期间更好地生存 = periods of drought。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: It has seen the return of native tree species.
items.zh: 这里恢复了一些本土树种。

items.en: It supports only one species of native monkey.
items.zh: 这里仅能养活一种本地猴。

items.en: Its monkey population helps the agriculture of the area.
items.zh: 当地猴群给农业带来了好处。

items.en: It is home to populations of all three local monkey species.
items.zh: 它是所有三种当地猴子的栖息地。

items.en: Its landscape was altered by the construction of a transport link.
items.zh: 由于建造了一条运输线路，其地貌发生了变化。

points: 这里明确提到从“对立” 转向“合作"一农民/商业活动的态度正在改变 (towards wildlife conservation).
能在干旱期间更好地生存 = periods of drought。
clauses: Studying such disturbed woodlands is increasingly important ….
连接词 because 引出“because throughout much of the New World Tropics, these are the only forests left”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
In the first 28 years following protection of the area, the capuchin population doubled, ….
连接词 while 引出“while the number of howlers increased seven-fold”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Rain-forest trees growing anew on Central American farmland are helping scientists find ways for monkey and agriculture to benefit one another.
在中美洲农田上重新生长的雨林正在帮助科学家找到使猴子和农业相互受益的方法。
